court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Ms.Kandan Hardware Mart vs /149 on 2 January, 2026

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ms.Kandan Hardware Mart, Represented by its Proprietor E.Palani
parties.respondent_defendant: The Assistant Commissioner (ST) (FAC), Park Town Assessment Circle, Chennai – 600 003.

facts_of_case: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to call for the impugned order dated 26.12.2022 and quash the same as passed in violation of principles of natural justice and contrary to law.

legal_principles.principle: Once a 'Late Fee' has been levied, there is no scope for levying the 'General Penalty' over and above.
legal_principles.held: The challenge to the 'General Penalty' by these Petitioners is that there is no scope for levying such 'Penalty' over and above the 'Late Fee', as the 'Late Fee' itself is penal in nature.
cited_cases: Tvl.Jainsons Castors and Industrial Products, Represented by its Authorized Representatives, Chennai Vs. The Assistant Commissioner (ST), Nandanam, Chennai vide order dated 04.02.2025 inW.P.No.36614 of 2024

legal_principles.principle: A 'Late Fee' is penal in nature.
legal_principles.held: The 'Late Fee' itself is penal in nature.

outcome.final_order: The Respondent is directed to rework the late fee in the light of Notification No.07/2023-Central Tax dated 31.03.2023 issued by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue), Government of India.
